content.text: {"headline":"Approve R2: the strongest policy-safe plan lifts disruption-window service level from 72.3% to 78.9%. That is still short of the 80% target, so it is the best available rather than a full fix.","why":"The surge comes from SMS campaign MKT-2026-825, sent at 10:15 to 700,000 people. Loan enquiries are running at 2.02x normal, and service level has already fallen to 41.3%. No plan that follows policy reaches 80% for 12:00-15:30. R2 gets closest at 78.9%, with abandons down from 6.6% to 4.5% and rest of day at 87.7%. It combines callbacks on both queues, 20% chat deflection, delayed payments breaks, overtime for 6 general agents from 14:45 to 15:45, cancelled payments coaching, and a move of 5 cross-skilled agents to general from 15:00. Extra cost is INR 1,938.","trade_offs":["Against R1: R2 costs INR 360 more (1,938 vs 1,578) for +1.5 points (78.9% vs 77.4%) and slightly fewer abandons (4.5% vs 4.8%).","P2 and P3 reach a similar level (77.9-78.1%) for little or no cost. Both break policy CX-01: they use a known-issue message, which needs a confirmed outage, and there is none here because the campaign is the cause. They are not usable.","General still lags at 74.1% while payments sits at 85.0%. Payments has headroom to give, so the move of 5 agents looks low-risk for that queue. However, payments also loses coaching and has breaks delayed by 45 minutes.","The no-cost option P1 gets only 73.7%, barely better than doing nothing (72.3%)."],"watch":"Watch general-queue service level and loan_enquiry volume after 12:00, and check whether the 6 overtime offers are accepted before 14:45. If general stays well below 74%, or the campaign drives a second wave, consider raising it with marketing or the duty manager."}
